source: Full audit of resources/[tarboro]/* on disk, diffed against server.cfg's ensure list, cross-checked against build memory. Re-run this diff any time a resource is added or removed to catch drift immediately.
caveat: Every resource below, including ones marked "good", has never been run by a real connected player. "good" means the build has a real narrative record and passed a boot test (all 60 running resources start cleanly with zero errors) — not that anyone has clicked the prompt, opened the menu, or walked the flow in-game. Status values: crit = not running at all, warn = thin or zero documentation, good = documented. Resources with a checks list can be marked tested behavior-by-behavior — a resource only shows fully tested once every one of its checks is checked.

items.name: tarboro-inventory
items.desc: Typed-slot layer on top of ox_inventory — the F2 panel (primary ×2, sidearm, melee, tool ×2, bag expansion), clothing-slot equip gating, and a Ground Items pickup panel.
items.note: FIXED 2026-08-10 — F2 opened the panel but couldn't close it (SetNuiFocus steals keyboard input from the native keybind once open). Added an F2 listener in html/slots.js alongside the existing Escape one. ADDED 2026-08-12 — auto-sort: the player's own inventory now sorts alphabetically and compacts into the lowest slots every time it's opened. NOTE this is a direct CODE edit to ox_inventory itself (server.lua: a SortPlayerInventory() function plus one call inside openInventory), not to a tarboro resource — so an ox_inventory update will silently wipe it, exactly like the custom item definitions. Both touch points and the re-apply steps are recorded in CUSTOM_ITEMS_AUDIT.md section 5. Scoped deliberately: player inventories only (stashes/shops/trunks are arranged on purpose), skipped while a bag is open, and inventory.weapon is remapped because it stores a SLOT NUMBER — sorting while armed without remapping would leave the server pointing at whatever item landed in the old slot. FIXED 2026-08-14 — GetSlotTypeForItem (shared/slots.lua) was calling exports.ox_inventory:Items() with NO argument on every occupied F2 slot on every grid fetch, returning the ENTIRE item registry each time — harmless at ~1,400 items but after the clothing-catalog merge pushed the registry to ~39,400 items (see tarboro-clothing's /gencatalog) this was the actual cause of "opening the inventory takes a minute." Fixed to pass the item name for an O(1) lookup — a direct regression caused by that catalog merge, not incidental, exactly the kind of case the standing optimization principles doc calls out. ADDED 2026-08-14 — equipment.lua extends the typed-slot system with one slot per ClothingSlots field (Config.ClothingSlotMax), so worn clothing is now gated through the same equip/limit machinery as weapons/tools. ADDED 2026-08-14/15 — Ground Items: F2 now shows nearby ox_inventory drops with a Pick Up action (getGroundItems callback, pickupGroundItem event, proximity re-validated server-side, refunds back to the drop if the player's inventory can't take it) — the Drop flow in reverse. FIXED 2026-08-14/15 — removed a defensive exports.ox_inventory:closeInventory() call that was silently telling the server to close the currently-open glovebox on any invOpen flip; this was the real cause of "glovebox stopped storing/retrieving items."

Stashes/trunks/gloveboxes/shops are NOT reordered — only your own inventory

items.name: tarboro-needs
items.desc: Hunger and thirst depletion with consumable items to restore them, gating the game's own passive health regeneration.
items.note: FIXED 2026-08-11 — eating/drinking did nothing at all. Root cause: item defs' `server = { event = 'tarboro:needs:consume' }` field was never real — ox_inventory doesn't read a per-item server.event, only the single global `ox_inventory:usedItem` event. Consumption is now hooked there directly, loading data/items.lua purely as a hungerRestore/thirstRestore lookup table. Debug print statements (`[tarboro-needs DEBUG] ...`) are still sitting in the handler — safe to strip once confirmed working live. SAFETY-CRITICAL FIX 2026-08-15 — vanilla GTA's own passive HP regen had NEVER been disabled anywhere in this codebase; it silently healed players regardless of hunger/thirst state, and is the likely root cause behind any past "bleed-out doesn't work" reports (regen could quietly pull a player back from near-fatal HP before ever crossing tarboro-death's downed threshold — see tarboro-death's own checks). Now disabled outright (SetPlayerHealthRechargeMultiplier(..., 0.0)), replaced with a new needs-gated regen loop that only heals while hunger AND thirst are both >= Config.NeedsRegenThreshold, skipping downed/dead players, plus a new low-key "getting low, go restock" nudge separate from the existing urgent <20 warning. New tarboro-config tunables: NeedsRegenThreshold/NeedsRegenTickSecs/NeedsRegenPerTick/NeedsNudgeThreshold/NeedsNudgeChance. Confirmed debug prints from the 2026-08-11 fix are fully gone.

checks.label: Hunger depletes over real time
Thirst depletes on its own timer, independent of hunger
HUD bars track the real values live, not stale/cached
Eating a food item restores hunger by the right amount (regression check for the fixed usedItem-wiring bug)

items.name: tarboro-property
items.desc: Real estate: browse/buy/rent, house interiors (16 of 31 assigned), player-named signs, vacant land + object placement, commercial storefronts, a real house_key item, and owner-initiated sell-back.
items.note: 2026-08-12 — furniture went from place-once/remove-only to a real place/MOVE/remove system. A new ghost-preview placer (client/placer.lua) lets you steer, rotate and confirm before committing, and is exported as StartPlacement() so tarboro-drugs reuses it cross-resource for its portable acid labs/sprinklers rather than building a second placement UI. Two things this fixed: (1) placement used to drop the prop at a fixed offset in front of you with no preview, and since the purchase happened on insert, a bad spot meant delete and RE-BUY — the charge now only lands after you confirm; (2) nothing placed could ever be repositioned. Moving is free, and the server re-validates that the destination is still inside the plot's manage radius, so furniture can't be walked off your land. NEW 2026-08-15 — buying a property now grants a real house_key ox_inventory item (metadata: listingKey/address), tracked in a new persistent tarboro_property_keys table (survives the owner going offline); selling revokes it (pulls the item live if online, deletes the DB row). Renting does NOT grant a house_key — confirmed no GrantPropertyKey call on the rent path, buy-only by design. The item is currently INERT — no lock/entry check anywhere in the codebase reads it yet, it's purely an inventory artifact for now. The old qb-houses "My Keys" ally-key-sharing tab was DROPPED, not replaced, on the reasoning that owning a property now always means holding the real item — there's no ally give/revoke UI for house_key the way tarboro-garage's vehicle_key just got. Also new: an owner-initiated sell-back (Config.PropertySellbackPct = 0.7) refunding 70% of listing price, clearing ownership/key, and re-listing the property, surfaced through the phone's Houses app. SAME PASS — client/land.lua's Manage Land UI (place/move/remove/update sign) moved from four nested context menus to one themed NUI panel; confirmed pure reskin, ghost-placement flow (SetNuiFocus false before placement) preserved, all four callbacks unchanged server-side. CRITICAL BUG, SAME-DAY FIX 2026-08-15 — server's tarboro:property:getMine was changed to send plain x/y instead of a raw coords vector3 (a vector3 doesn't reliably survive the NUI JSON bridge, which broke the Houses app's GPS button — see tarboro-phone). That change silently broke client/main.lua's loadMine(): it still read p.coords.x, which was now nil, throwing "attempt to index a nil value" on the FIRST owned property and aborting the rest of the loop — meaning NO blip, NO rename/land-manage interact, and critically NO Enter-door interact ever got registered for ANY owned or rented property. A freshly bought house had no door prompt at all. Fixed same day by reading the listing's own local static coords (shared_script data, already on the client) instead of the server-sent p.coords. The identical root cause also broke tarboro-business's Register Business prompt and tarboro-garage's Park Here prompt (both fixed the same way, same day — see those entries).

items.name: tarboro-garage
items.desc: Take-out/store at 9 public garages, plus physical driveway vehicle slots on owned properties AND 4 open-access Public Lots — parked cars are real, stealable (unless locked), persistent entities with an owner/ally/key-holder unlock system.
items.note: NEW 2026-08-14 — extended the existing driveway-slot system (unchanged core, §7 2026-08-10) with: (1) 4 Public Lots (Downtown 8 slots, Vinewood Hills 6, Sandy Shores 6, Del Perro 6) using the identical Park Here mechanism, no property ownership required; (2) every slot-parked vehicle now spawns door-locked and frozen (private always; public lots only if that vehicle's own lock_in_public_lots toggle is on, default on) — only the owner, a tarboro-allies ally, or a vehicle_key holder can unlock (keybind N, 5s window, auto-relocks if nobody gets in; getting in the driver seat unfreezes it); (3) a new persistent tarboro_vehicle_keys table makes the vehicle_key item a real access grant an owner can hand to a specific ally via the phone's Garage app (Give/Revoke), independent of the broader ally relationship, surviving pull-outs, reset only by explicit revoke or auto-impound. New columns on player_vehicles: parked_property_key/parked_slot/parked_vehicle_type, lock_in_public_lots. EXPLICITLY NOT BUILT YET (resource's own comment): real walk-in garage interiors — every property still ships as a driveway slot, nothing has garageType='interior'. Slot/public-lot coordinates are computed/approximate, not measured — same caveat as every other placeholder-coords system in this project. SAME PASS — UI (html/main.*) merged the nested root→Take Out/Ally/Store menu into one themed tabbed panel; behavior unchanged, all server calls (getMyVehicles, getMyAllies, getAllyVehicles, takeOut, storeVehicle) still present. FIXED 2026-08-15 (same root cause as tarboro-property/tarboro-business) — client/property_slots.lua's private "Park Here" interact zone read p.coords from tarboro:property:getMine, which now only sends plain x/y; the zone's coords was always nil, so it never actually covered the driveway. Fixed to use the listing's own local static coords instead. Public Lot "Park Here" zones were unaffected (they never depended on getMine).

items.name: tarboro-drugs
items.desc: 5-tier legal weed economy (cash payout), acid (replaces meth), coke, and crack verticals; baggie-gated packaging; a grow-op placeables layer (portable acid labs, sprinklers, watering can); random reachability-validated air drops.
items.note: MAJOR BUG FOUND+FIXED 2026-08-10 — the entire 5-tier weed/acid item rework had never actually been merged into ox_inventory's real item registry, so none of those items could be granted at all. Fixed: 16 missing items added, 5 stale old-strain items removed, item count went 308→319 exactly matching the math. Real coords for the Vinewood Hills (crimson) forage area also walked in and swapped in for the old placeholders. EXPANDED 2026-08-12 — three new subsystems: (1) Placeables — acid_lab_kit ($4500, worse batch/purity than every fixed station on purpose so it can't obsolete them) and sprinkler ($220), placeable only on owned property, reusing tarboro-property's ghost-placer via a cross-resource StartPlacement() export rather than building a second placement UI. (2) Watering — watering_can ($45) + sprinklers accelerate grow time (capped total boost per plant) but a plant can never die or stall from neglect by design. (3) Air drops — replaces the old fixed CokeDropZones; one generic system for both chem_precursor and coke_brick_raw, candidates ring-picked around a random online player and validated by a real client (ground/water/interior checks) before the crate exists, first-come-first-served. ACID VERTICAL REWORKED 2026-08-12 — (a) blotter paper is now a real recipe input, not flavour: acid_raw + paper + baggie -> tabs, matching how LSD is actually dosed (paper $8 at the 24/7). (b) Tabs can be made TWO ways — at a bagging station (2s) or in hand anywhere by using Blotter Paper (6s, slower on purpose so the station still has a reason to exist); both fire the SAME server recipe so they can't drift apart or be played against each other. (c) Tabs of Acid is now consumable from the inventory context menu — a ~2min trip cycling four stock GTA timecycles with drunk-cam wobble, which always tears down on death/respawn/resource-stop so nobody can get stuck tripping. (d) PURITY NOW AFFECTS VALUE, not just volume: a clean cook at a station with real glassware returns a share of its output as high-grade (acid_raw_pure -> acid_packaged_pure, $340 vs the standard $200). Tier 2 = 40% high grade, Tier 3 = 100%, portable lab = never (its 0.85 multiplier sits below the threshold by design). Previously the skill check and station tier only scaled the COUNT, so a flawless Superlab cook and a botched RV cook sold for exactly the same price. The yield maths is shared by both cook paths on purpose — a discrepancy there would be an exploit (cook wherever pays better), not just a bug. (e) The three cook stations finally have map blips; they were the one part of any vertical you had to already know the coordinates of to find. UI (2026-08-15) — the Bagging Station, Trapping's serve-customer sale, /myplants status, and placeable object actions all moved to one themed html/bagging.* panel; confirmed 1:1 behavior, all four SHOW_* message types handled.
